Facts to look for:
[R1] Fact: Never modify anything under src/legacy/. Reason: it is vendored from the old logistics monolith and the platform team's sync job overwrites the folder every Monday, so changes are silently lost.
    Rubric: 2 = Names src/legacy/ AND gives the reason (vendored / overwritten by the weekly sync, changes lost). | 1 = Names src/legacy/ without a (correct) reason.
[R2] Fact: No new npm dependencies at all, not even dev dependencies. Reason: every new package needs a security review that takes about six weeks.
    Rubric: 2 = No new dependencies (incl. dev) AND the security-review reason. | 1 = No new dependencies, but no or wrong reason (or omits that dev deps are included AND gives no reason).
[R3] Fact: GET /shipments/:id must not change in any way. Reason: the mobile app v2.3 parses it with a strict schema and crashes on unknown or missing fields; their next release is in January.
    Rubric: 2 = Names GET /shipments/:id AND the mobile-app strict-parsing reason. | 1 = Names GET /shipments/:id without the reason, or the reason with a vague/wrong endpoint.
[R4] Fact: New user-facing error messages (`message`) must be in German, because the warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim to the packers. The `code` field stays English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.
    Rubric: 2 = German messages AND (the reason: warehouse staff UI shows them verbatim, OR the English SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE code convention). | 1 = German messages only, with neither reason nor code convention.
[R5] Fact: Never log the recipient's name, address or phone number (personal data). Reason: GDPR; the data protection officer flagged exactly this in last month's audit. Shipment IDs and tracking numbers are fine.
    Rubric: 2 = Recipient personal data (name/address/phone or 'recipient PII') AND GDPR/DPO/audit reason. | 1 = Recipient personal data without a reason, or a generic 'no PII' without saying recipient data.
[D1] Fact: Austrian public holidays for 2026 and 2027 are a hardcoded list in src/services/holidays.ts (no holiday API). Reason: the warehouse deployment has no outbound internet access, so it must work fully offline.
    Rubric: 2 = Hardcoded/static list (no API) AND the no-outbound-internet / offline reason. | 1 = Hardcoded list without the reason.
[D2] Fact: Max 3 attempts in total, fixed 30-second delay, no exponential backoff. Reason: the ERP deduplicates by event_id only within a 2-minute window, so all attempts must land within 2 minutes or duplicates are created.
    Rubric: 2 = 3 attempts + fixed 30 s / no backoff AND the 2-minute dedup-window reason. | 1 = Correct parameters without the reason, or the reason with partly wrong parameters.
[D3] Fact: No. Keep the JSON file store (writes are debounced at 200 ms instead). Reason: ops backs up data/store.json with a nightly rsync job that diffs plain-text files; a binary SQLite file would break their backup checks.
    Rubric: 2 = Keep JSON / no SQLite AND the ops rsync/plain-text backup reason. | 1 = Keep JSON / no SQLite without the (correct) reason.
[D4] Fact: Only ATP (Austrian Post) numbers are validated, as UPU S10 incl. mod-11 check digit. All other carriers: any non-empty value. Reason: their formats change too often; last year valid DHL numbers were rejected for two days.
    Rubric: 2 = ATP-only S10/check-digit validation, others accept anything non-empty, AND the 'formats change too often / DHL incident' reason. | 1 = ATP-only validation without the reason.
[X1] Fact: fs.watch was tried and never fires on staging, because the config is a Docker bind mount from a Windows host and file change events don't propagate into the container. Polling with fs.watchFile worked.
    Rubric: 2 = fs.watch fails AND why (Docker bind mount / events don't propagate); mentioning fs.watchFile polling as what works is expected but not required. | 1 = Only one part: 'fs.watch doesn't work' without the reason, or 'use fs.watchFile polling' without the failure explanation.
[X2] Fact: In the JSON body as top-level field `sig` (computed over the body without `sig`). An `X-Signature` header was tried first and failed because the ERP's API gateway strips all custom X- headers.
    Rubric: 2 = Body field `sig` AND header was tried AND the gateway strips custom X- headers. | 1 = Partial: body `sig` only, or 'header didn't work' without the gateway reason.
[X3] Fact: Yes. Memoizing calculateEta caused stale ETAs: after a new tracking event (e.g. an exception) the list kept the old ETA because the cache wasn't invalidated; a proper cache key got messy. The memoization was removed; ETA caching is a dead end (paginate the list instead).
    Rubric: 2 = Tried AND stale ETAs after new events / invalidation problem AND removed (dead end). | 1 = Tried and removed without the reason, or the staleness problem without saying it was abandoned.
[X4] Fact: No. Batching was tried (September): the ERP answers 422 to any array payload and only accepts a single event object per request.
    Rubric: 2 = No AND the ERP rejects arrays (422) / single object only. | 1 = No, without the reason.
[F1] Fact: Port 9911 (since the October infra move). The docs and README still say 8080, which is outdated.
    Rubric: 2 = 9911. | 1 = Mentions 9911 but hedges between 9911 and 8080.
[F2] Fact: 'emits webhook on delivered' in test/events.test.ts fails about 1 in 5 runs on CI (timer race), tracked as OPS-412, owned by the platform team. If it fails: rerun once, don't try to fix it.
    Rubric: 2 = Names the test ('emits webhook on delivered' or clearly the delivered-webhook test in events.test.ts) AND 'rerun once / don't fix it'. | 1 = Names the test without the handling, or the handling with only a vague test reference.
